Often I think about how to prepare, what supplies will be available, what supplies will still have distribution and in what time frame they will become distributed after certain events, and also what supplies will other people be short on and overlook. All those questions depend on a premise of things not traveling to point A to point B or people being so tied down with emergency response that they don't show up to work so item B never turns into item C.

There is a lot that is imported into your home. Water, electricity, food. And there are a lot of things that don't run without those things not only in your home but outside of it. Meat doesn't store. Sources of protein become scarce.

Well I have an answer of a scale to think about and that is one town or one city. Think about the environment surrounding your home as just being the functions that a town can sustain itself, while under dysfunctional circumstances so about 10% of what could work in a single town will work.

Why a town or a city. Because I like to look to actual events for decision making. We are very pampered in the US to the point that people can laugh at preppers but the circumstances we prepare for are real world life and events for other people on the planet. Not 50 years ago but today. For example people may laugh at collecting food but all war when fought on your land instead of across the ocean produces famine. For example ~600 people may have died of starvation this week due to war-related starvation in Syria. This is normal circumstances that all geographies of the world have faced in the last 100 years except the US you need to go back about 170 years.

So why a city based on real world emergency circumstances. Because it is not uncommon for towns to be blocked off at the town level. It takes about a day to fully fence a city of about any size. The bigger it is the more arcs your run in parallel. You could get it done in twelve.

Here is a Marine article on Victory Through Logistics: http://www.1stmlg.marines.mil/News/News-Article-Display/Article/542943/barrier-around-fallujah-intended-to-stop-insurgents-supplies-mobility/

Here is fencing around Fallujah: http://media.gettyimages.com/photos/fallujah-iraq-us-marines-from-the-2nd-battalion-6th-marines-regiment-picture-id56449761

If there ever is war cities will be locked down because you want to reduce your enemy's mobility even if civilian mobility is reduced. Even the noblest of sides can think of citizens as cattle which are best kept safe in difficult circumstances. If they can't wonder off that's all the better for them. Fuck to freedom of movement or the fact that your life's sustainment depends on other people's freedom of movement today. We can read about this same circumstance in Syria under Assad: http://www.aljazeera.com/news/2016/01/400000-syrians-hungry-besieged-areas-160110060836705.html

I want to clarify. I'm not making any value judgments about any side of any conflict. This is just the logistics of war that we've seen put into place in two different theaters by two different actors. This is standard operations whether it is the good guys in charge or the bad guys in charge.

The assumption that we will continue to be the exception and be able to turn our 170 years into 300 years without famine producing conflict is a very interesting form of vanity on our part. The law of independent odds suggests that we are more likely to follow the trend for the rest of the Earth and our past luck is insignificant. Famine producing conflict in your lifetime is normal.
